result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.floyd_warshall()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Compute all-pairs shortest-path distances with the Floyd-Warshall algorithm. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.floyd_warshall()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Compute all-pairs shortest-path distances with the Floyd-Warshall algorithm. title: >- [Graph.floyd_warshall()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Compute all-pairs shortest-path distances with the Floyd-Warshall algorithm. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute all-pairs shortest-path distances with the Floyd-Warshall algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L54190-L54265){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.floyd_warshall( weighted=None, return_predecessors=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Floyd-Warshall distances](/assets/graphs/floyd-warshall.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three nodes with directed weighted edges A to B 4, A to C 2 and C to B −1. The negative shortcut makes the long way round, A, C, B (accent color), cheaper than the direct edge: 2 + (−1) = 1. The distance matrix highlights dist A to B = 1.0; pairs with no path, such as B to A, are left out (shown as a dot)." width="100%"} Floyd-Warshall fills in the full table of shortest distances between every pair of nodes. Unlike `all_pairs_shortest_path_length()`, it accepts negative edge weights (as long as no cycle has negative total weight), which arise with costs that can be gains, such as profits, log-probabilities or energy recovery. It is also a compact choice for small, dense graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. [return_predecessors]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, also return `pred[source][target]`, the node before `target` on a shortest path from `source`, from which any path can be rebuilt. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or tuple]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `dist[source][target]` for every reachable pair (each node at distance `0` from itself; unreachable pairs are omitted). With `return_predecessors=True`, a `(dist, pred)` pair. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph has a negative cycle (or an undirected graph has a negative edge). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The triple loop $d(i, j) \leftarrow \min(d(i, j), d(i, k) + d(k, j))$ over every intermediate node $k$ takes $O(V^3)$ time and $O(V^2)$ memory, independent of the number of edges; for sparse graphs with negative weights, `johnson()` is faster. A negative diagonal entry reveals a negative cycle. Distances match NetworkX's `floyd_warshall` (which also lists unreachable pairs as infinity). ## Examples {.doc-examples} A shortcut with a negative cost makes the long way round the cheapest: ::: {#2539c072 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B", 4.0), ("A", "C", 2.0), ("C", "B", -1.0)]) dist = g.floyd_warshall() dist[g.get_id_from_label("A")][g.get_id_from_label("B")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: :::
